clue.text: Kept going from the sun to the shade

indicators.note: taking only the opening letter from the word sun, its initial being what is drawn from it

parts.note: taken as written
red is a shade, or colour

explanation.surface: Something kept was moved out of the sunshine into the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the' takes just the first letter of 'sun'; 'going' and the second 'the' only link the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored goods are kept in reserve, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Friendly and gracious face!

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'goodness gracious!'
dial is slang for a person's face, as well as a clock face

explanation.surface: Someone with a warm, gracious expression is praised as friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' looks like a second adjective beside 'Friendly', but it stands for the exclamation COR, as in 'gracious me!'. DIAL is old British slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial welcome is a warm and friendly one, a synonym.

clue.text: The out train isn't on it's way

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A passenger remarks that the outbound train has not yet left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of TRAIN and ISNT into a two-word phrase; the apostrophes in the clue give no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in transit are travelling between places, i.e. under way.

clue.text: Getting the gist, somehow — mother is in disgrace

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of gist are arranged in some other manner

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Grasping the point at last, someone learns their mother has been shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges GIST into STIG, and MA follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or dishonour, a synonym.

clue.text: Little creatures by an upturned stone

parts.note: the word read as 'up turned' gives the two letters of up in reverse order
mice are small creatures

explanation.surface: Tiny animals scurry out from under a stone that has been turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' is read cryptically as UP turned round, giving PU, which MICE stand 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light, porous volcanic rock used for scrubbing skin.

clue.text: Retain halfthe money netted by a false claim

indicators.note: netted by means caught inside, so the money surrounds the other piece

parts.note: pence are British coins, small sums of money

indicators.note: half asks for the first half of the word retain, its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps half the takings, caught out by a fraudulent claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes RET from RETAIN, and 'netted by' puts it inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a show put on to deceive, so a false claim or sham.

clue.text: Doctor, tea or coffee?

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A doctor asks a patient whether they would like tea or coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee, named after the Yemeni port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Will a bloke fall apart through this foolish infatuation

indicators.note: apart means the letters fall to pieces and are reassembled

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a bloke or chap

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man will be ruined by a silly crush.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is old British slang for a man; 'apart' rearranges COVE and FALL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf love is a youthful, short-lived romantic crush.

clue.text: Accepted the money, one observed

parts.note: took means received or accepted
a note is one piece of paper money

explanation.surface: A clerk who took the cash noticed something.
explanation.definitionFit: To take note of something is to notice or observe it, an idiom.

clue.text: They may be responsible for raised eyebrows!

definitions.text: They may be responsible for raised eyebrows!

parts.words: They may be responsible for raised eyebrows!
parts.note: surprise raises eyebrows, but here the eyebrows are drawn on, raised by make-up sticks

explanation.walkthrough: 'raised eyebrows' suggests surprise; it means eyebrows given shape by cosmetic drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebrow pencils are cosmetic sticks used to draw or define brows.

clue.text: Qualification, perhaps, for a trooper

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to qualify a statement, and a cavalry trooper rides a horse.

clue.text: Unhappy and clutching a woolly bear, mustered a smile

indicators.note: woolly suggests a fuzzy, muddled state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sad child hugs a fluffy teddy and manages to smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' jumbles BEAR together with SMILE; 'mustered a' is only scene-setting link.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable means wretchedly unhappy, a synonym.

clue.text: Beside oneself again with rage

parts.note: I is the speaker's own self
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone is beside themselves with fury once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beside oneself' is the idiom for fury, but here 'Beside' just places I next to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger or wrath, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Attracted by, are prepared to approach

parts.note: drawn means pulled towards, attracted

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of are are reworked

explanation.surface: People drawn in by something are ready to come closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges ARE into EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw near is to come close, an idiom for approach.

clue.text: Cut the key and go

parts.note: C is a musical key
leave means depart, go

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a door key and departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split or chop through, a synonym.

clue.text: Aiming to have an evening out

explanation.definitionFit: Levelling a gun is pointing it, and levelling ground is making it flat and even.

clue.text: As an enemy deserter, I'm interned temporarily

indicators.note: interned means confined within, so the enemy holds the following pieces

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a rat is one who deserts, as rats desert a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A soldier who deserted to the enemy says he is held in a camp for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interned' places RAT and IM inside FOE.
explanation.definitionFit: For a time means for a while, not permanently.

clue.text: Rocks constituting a hazard to shipping

explanation.definitionFit: Whisky 'on the rocks' is served with cubes of frozen water, and icebergs threaten vessels.

clue.text: Agree, for money, to roll the dice

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

indicators.note: rolling dice tumbles them, so their letters are tumbled too

explanation.surface: A gambler agrees to throw the dice for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to roll' rearranges DICE into CIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions that coincide agree or correspond exactly.

clue.text: Said it's a drink stand

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the drink's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A remark that a drink is being offered at a stall.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf ball is placed on a little peg before driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee is the small peg on which a golf ball stands for the first stroke.

clue.text: Cover in also in the greenhouse

indicators.note: in places the cover inside the other word

parts.note: too means also
a mat is a floor cover

explanation.surface: Instructions to cover something up in the greenhouse as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MAT inside TOO; the definition is a cryptic description of something grown under glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are a classic crop grown in greenhouses, so the definition describes one by example.

clue.text: Before getting up, as well

indicators.note: in a down clue read upwards the letters still say the same word, so it reads either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A note about something happening before rising from bed, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up, as well' says the answer still reads the same going up the grid as down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is an archaic word for before.

clue.text: Feeling for the book-stand, on I totter

indicators.note: totter means wobble unsteadily, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A sentimental attachment to a bookstand, voiced by someone unsteady on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totter' rearranges TOME with ON and I; '-stand' merely completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or fear, a synonym.

clue.text: Think the grass border made up for it

indicators.note: border means surround, so the grass flanks the other word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
deem means think or judge

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the grass edging compensated for a flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a garden edging, but works as a verb: REED borders DEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a fault is to make amends or compensate for it.

clue.text: Slips the animal into the time capsule

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the animal goes within the time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Instructions to slip an animal into a buried time capsule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts RAT inside ERA, which 'capsule' completes as the container in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing errors, or slips, listed in a book.

clue.text: Mean to turn in-need regeneration

indicators.note: regeneration means renewing or remaking, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An instruction about meaning to turn something in need of renewal around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regeneration' rearranges TO and NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or indicate, a synonym of mean.

clue.text: A local worker

parts.note: suggests someone employed nearby, but a local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is your nearest pub, so its worker serves drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves drinks in a pub, which Britons call their local.

clue.text: Foot the bill? It's a pleasure!

explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone a meal is to pay for it, and a special delight is something enjoyed.

clue.text: What Perdita was lost in

parts.note: Perdita, the abandoned princess of Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale, has a name meaning lost in the old Roman tongue

explanation.walkthrough: Perdita looks like a story about where she was lost; it asks which language her name means 'lost' in.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdita is the feminine of perditus, 'lost', in the Roman language.

clue.text: When the wind is backing, be inside. It's very cold

indicators.note: inside places the word be within the others
a backing wind shifts anticlockwise, so here the words are read backwards

parts.note: air is a wind or breeze

explanation.surface: Advice to stay indoors when the wind changes direction, because it is freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AIR and IS into SIRIA, and 'inside' puts BE after SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is a vast Russian region famed for bitterly cold winters.

clue.text: Be different from the others and get a porter to carry

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the beer holds the other word

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a type of stout

explanation.surface: Someone stands out by hiring a hotel porter to carry their bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a baggage handler, but it is a dark beer; 'to carry' puts AND inside STOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to be conspicuous or distinct from others.

clue.text: Get one's goat some greenery

explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to get their goat, and the stinging plant is a common weed.
